clue.text: Pulled back, looking strained and below par

parts.note: a drawn face looks tired and strained
feeling off means feeling unwell, below par

explanation.surface: A golfer withdraws, looking tense and playing worse than par.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Below par' suggests golf scores, but here it means feeling unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Curtains or troops withdrawn are pulled back; the phrasal verb means extracted or retracted.

clue.text: Stern nurse

definitions.meaning: the stern is the back part of a ship
to nurse a child is to bring it up, raise it

explanation.definitionFit: The back of a ship is its hindmost part, and bringing up a child is raising it.

clue.text: Resist having a rest

parts.note: with means having, as in a man with a hat
a stand is a support or rest for something

explanation.surface: Someone tired refuses to sit down and take a break.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold out against an attack or pressure is to oppose it successfully.

clue.text: Exercises barely accepted in public

indicators.note: accepted means taken in, so one piece is placed within the other here

parts.note: barely means only, as in only just
PE is physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: Gym workouts done with very little clothing in front of others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barely' hints at nudity in the gym, but is just a synonym; 'accepted' signals that the exercises go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something without concealment means doing it where all can see.

clue.text: Person in the same boat who sympathised with the Russians?

definitions.meaning: a companion on the same journey, literally sharing the trip
a Communist sympathiser who was not a party member

explanation.definitionFit: Literally a companion on a journey; figuratively a Cold War term for a non-member who shared Communist views.

clue.text: Has desire to catch wild animals

indicators.note: to catch means to enclose, so one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: taken as written
a yen is a longing or desire

explanation.surface: A hunter wants to trap some animals in the wild.
explanation.definitionFit: These scavenging carnivores of Africa and Asia are untamed beasts.

clue.text: Such a charge may well be ordinary

definitions.text: Such a charge may well be ordinary

parts.words: Such a charge may well be ordinary
parts.note: in coats of arms an ordinary is a simple geometric charge such as a bend or chevron

explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' and 'ordinary' look like a bill or accusation being commonplace, but both are terms from coats of arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to coats of arms, where charges (devices on a shield) include the simple ordinaries.

clue.text: Encouraged, say, by good editor

parts.note: e.g. means for example, which say can also mean

explanation.surface: A kind editor gave a writer some encouragement.
explanation.definitionFit: Urged on, as in spurring someone to act.

clue.text: Not voting for self-denying ordinance

definitions.meaning: declining to cast a vote either way
a rule of refraining from indulgence, such as avoiding drink

explanation.definitionFit: Refraining from voting, or the practice of refraining from pleasures such as alcohol.

clue.text: When dining, it was socially divisive

definitions.text: When dining, it was socially divisive

parts.words: When dining, it was socially divisive
parts.note: at old banquets guests of high rank sat above the table's salt dish and lesser people below it

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'below the salt' meant being seated among the lower-status diners.
explanation.definitionFit: The salt container on a medieval table marked the divide between honoured and humbler guests.

clue.text: Outbreak of wind from sulphur in alimentary canal

indicators.note: in places the element symbol inside the word for the digestive tract

parts.note: the gut is the alimentary canal
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: Flatulence with a sulphurous smell from the digestive tract.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about flatulence; the definition is weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden blast of moving air is a brief outburst of breeze.

clue.text: Add one small change to river that will help fish upstream

indicators.note: change tells us to rearrange these letters into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An engineer suggests a minor alteration to a river so fish can swim up it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small change' looks like loose coins, but 'change' alone is the anagram signal working on the three words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A series of stepped pools built beside a weir lets migrating fish climb past it.

clue.text: Employment requiring commitment to union

definitions.meaning: a job or hiring, as in a booking for a performer
a betrothal, a promise to marry

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a job or hiring and the period of being betrothed before marriage.

clue.text: Little Asian money once for a royal governess out East

definitions.meaning: a former Indian coin worth one sixteenth of a rupee
... Leonowens was governess to the children of the King of Siam

explanation.definitionFit: A small former coin of India, and the name of the governess in The King and I.

clue.text: Follow and pass, or drive just behind

parts.note: to tail someone is to follow them closely
a gate can be a pass or gap through mountains

explanation.surface: Advice on overtaking, or on staying close behind another car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass' looks like overtaking but means a mountain gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Motorists who sit too close to the car in front are said to do this.

clue.text: With tragic going, doth bid farewell thus to sweet prince

definitions.text: With tragic going, doth bid farewell thus to sweet prince

parts.words: With tragic going, doth bid farewell thus to sweet prince
parts.note: at Hamlet's death Horatio takes leave of him with the words that begin his famous line

explanation.walkthrough: Horatio's farewell in Hamlet is the line ending 'sweet prince'.
explanation.definitionFit: A parting phrase spoken at bedtime, used by Horatio for the dying Hamlet.

clue.text: Become calm and compromise

parts.note: to calm down is to stop being cross; end means stop
anger is the crossness that stops

explanation.surface: Advice to settle down and reach a middle ground in an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the phrase as 'end anger', stop being cross; 'compromise' is the verb meaning put at risk.
explanation.definitionFit: To compromise safety is to put it in peril.

clue.text: Plant in cultivated area with excellent return

parts.note: a garden is a piece of cultivated land

indicators.note: return means the letters for excellent come back the other way

parts.note: A1 (written AI) means first-class, excellent

explanation.surface: A plant grown in tended ground gives a fine yield.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragrant white-flowered evergreen shrub.

clue.text: Originally, only Bank of England could be source of notes

indicators.note: originally means at first, so the first letter of the next word is used

parts.note: BoE is the abbreviation for the Bank of England

explanation.surface: Only the central bank could issue banknotes in the beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notes' suggests banknotes, but means musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodwind instrument produces musical tones.

clue.text: A team's words missed by the other players

definitions.text: words missed by the other players

parts.note: a side is a team, and the possessive 's supplies the final S

explanation.surface: Remarks from one sports team that the opposing players fail to hear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Players' looks like sport but means actors; an actor speaks these to the audience, unheard by others on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarks made on stage to the audience, supposedly unheard by the other characters.

clue.text: Dines with a select combination from this?

definitions.text: Dines with a select combination from this?

indicators.note: combination says these letters are put together in a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone eats a choice mix of foods from a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'combination' rearranges DINES, A and SELECT; the whole clue also describes buying a mixed meal from such a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop selling cooked meats and fine prepared foods from which a picnic can be assembled.

clue.text: Odd expression of fool taking time off to get married

indicators.note: taking with off to get means one letter is removed and another put in its place
with taking, this signals removal of one letter and insertion of another

parts.note: an idiot is a fool

explanation.surface: A foolish person pauses from work to wed.
explanation.walkthrough: Replace T in IDIOT with M.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase whose meaning cannot be worked out from its words is a peculiar turn of speech.

clue.text: "Kismet" announced as the outdoor entertainment

indicators.note: announced means spoken, so the word is the one heard rather than written

parts.note: kismet is destiny, fate

explanation.surface: The musical Kismet is advertised as an open-air show.
explanation.walkthrough: Kismet is also a musical, which the quotes suggest.
explanation.definitionFit: A summer garden party or village fair with stalls held outside.

clue.text: No end of a risk for Iolanthe, perhaps

indicators.note: no end of means the final letter of the following word is dropped

parts.note: peril is risk or danger

explanation.surface: No end of danger for the heroine of a Gilbert and Sullivan opera.
explanation.walkthrough: Iolanthe is the fairy heroine of a Gilbert and Sullivan opera; 'perhaps' marks her as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A Persian fairy or sprite, which the title character of that opera is.

clue.text: Californian prospector — or Australian?

parts.note: a miner in the 1849 rush; an Australian soldier is also nicknamed a digger

explanation.walkthrough: Besides the miner, the phrase also means someone who courts the wealthy for money.
explanation.definitionFit: A miner hunting precious metal in a nineteenth-century rush; digger is also slang for an Australian.

clue.text: Keeper missing start of play is a dud

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so a letter is taken away from the keeper

parts.note: a stumper is a wicket-keeper in cricket, who guards the stumps

indicators.note: start of means only the opening letter of play is used

explanation.surface: A goalkeeper who misses the kick-off is useless.
explanation.walkthrough: A wicket-keeper stands behind the stumps in cricket. Remove P from STUMPER. Stumer is slang for a counterfeit or a failure.
explanation.definitionFit: Old slang for a forged cheque or a worthless thing, a failure.

clue.text: Standard form of stereo accepted by engineers

indicators.note: accepted by means taken inside, so the engineers' letters enclose the rest

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

indicators.note: form of means the letters of the next word take a new shape

explanation.surface: A standard design of hi-fi approved by technicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form of' gives OSETRE from STEREO, which 'accepted by' puts inside RE. A standard is a shrub trained on a single tall stem.
explanation.definitionFit: A rose grafted onto a tall upright stem is called a standard.
